Song Pack Studio

Import songs for Retro Music Player v2.9.01. Add audio, match timed lyrics, and export a Minecraft-ready Songs .mcaddon. Audio files are processed on your device.

Compatible with Retro Music Player v2.9.01 (also v2.8.29–2.8.31) and Retro Karaoke Stage v1.0.4. New content-ID exports require these updated add-ons. Existing older song packs still work in them. Native TTML is included as original XML; a legacy eLRC fallback is included when it fits. The build log reports whether TTML has word timing and background vocals. Install and enable the base Behavior Pack and Resource Pack first. This tool builds a separate Songs Behavior Pack + Songs Resource Pack that communicates with the base add-on. Download Retro Music Player on CurseForge

Importing songs does not change the already-installed base add-on; Minecraft still needs the generated Songs packs enabled in your world.

Vorbis OGG files work offline without conversion. Other supported formats use a converter loaded over the internet. Browser codec support varies.
Use matching filenames for automatic lyrics. If filenames or a unique track number cannot pair them, Studio checks both Artist and Title against lyric metadata when available. TTML is converted automatically to timed LRC/eLRC; overlapping vocals and translations cannot be displayed separately.

Creates a Minecraft-ready .mcaddon file

Identical source audio files share a content ID, even if renamed. Higher priority wins; equal priority uses first registration. Different files with the same name remain separate. Re-encoded or retagged audio may have different IDs.

Pack ID:

Save this identity before moving browsers/devices. Rebuild with the same identity to update this pack. New identity creates a separate pack.

Only enable when rebuilding an old pack with its original audio and filenames. Import the complete original collection first; add new songs in a later build. Save the updated identity after exporting. Old packs already installed do not need migration. For the latest lyrics features, use Retro Music Player v2.8.29 or newer / Karaoke v1.0.4 or newer.

Q6 is a Vorbis quality setting, not 320 kbps. Q9 is approximately 320 kbps for typical stereo music; bitrate varies. Re-encoding MP3/AAC is lossy and cannot improve the source. For large WAV/FLAC files, high-quality compressed audio (such as a 320 kbps source or Q9 export) is often much smaller; audible differences depend on the source, equipment and listener. Q6 uses less space. Large collections require more device memory and longer imports.

Both generated packs include the Retro Music Player icon by default. A custom square PNG replaces it.

Alternative installation: If your iPad or Minecraft will not import the combined Songs .mcaddon, download and import both individual packs below.

Download Songs Behavior Pack (.mcpack) Download Songs Resource Pack (.mcpack)

Install in Minecraft Bedrock

  1. Download Retro Music Player v2.9.01 from CurseForge. Import the base .mcaddon into Minecraft and enable its Behavior Pack + Resource Pack.
  2. Click Build songs for v2.9.01 to export your custom Songs packs.
  3. Open the downloaded .mcaddon with Minecraft.
  4. In world settings, enable all four packs: Retro Music Player BP, Retro Music Player RP, Songs BP, and Songs RP. Then fully exit and reopen the world.

On iPad: save the exported file in Files, then choose Share → Minecraft if available. If importing the combined Songs file fails, use the separate .mcpack downloads shown after building. If your browser changes the extension to .zip, rename it to .mcaddon (or .mcpack) before importing.

Every song you add shows up in the recording deck’s song list, where you record it onto a blank MiniDisc. No song is tied to a disc number and up to 1,000 songs can be imported per pack; up to 16 named packs can register; each MZ-RH1 holds up to 300 loaded tracks.
New exports use content-based song IDs: keep the original audio file unchanged when rebuilding to preserve existing disc references. For older filename-based discs, use the migration option with the original filenames. Display titles can still be changed in game. To change songs later, keep the pack identity, rebuild and import the updated Songs pack; select its latest version in world settings if Minecraft keeps the old version.
Only use music you own or have permission to use.
